whatThisRecordIs: The public-safe aggregate of an inventory built entirely in a separate private workspace. Every figure here is a count over material this repository does not hold and may not hold. The files those counts came from are bound below by digest, which is the whole of the binding available: a digest names bytes without disclosing them, and a reader outside the private workspace can confirm that a figure was computed over the bytes named here only by being given those bytes.

graph.blockedNodeReason: declared no dependency metadata, so the node exists and its edges are unknown rather than absent

readObservation.watches: four methods of Python's zipfile — namelist, infolist, open and ZipExtFile.read — and the unzip binary, shimmed ahead of the real one on PATH
readObservation.bound: This observes reads through the two channels it wraps. It does not establish that they are the only channels, and the premise that they were is a claim that has already been falsified once: an independent reviewer added a reader using only the standard library through an unwrapped channel, decompressed entry bodies to disk, and the observation printed zero entry bodies read and exited zero. So the figure below is what was seen through the watched channels, and metadata-only is an observed property of those channels rather than a proved property of the run. What it is not is a declaration nobody checked, which is what it replaced.
readObservation.notWatched: reads of files that are not archives — the pinned manifest, the acquisition log, the workspace's own tracked files, and the pack override tree

judgedClaims.claim: the licence family each distinct declared licence string belongs to
judgedClaims.recordedIn: a tracked table of one row per distinct declared string
judgedClaims.whyNoSecondReading: nothing about a licence is derivable from the artifact it governs, so a mutation changing the classifying code and the table together passes

judgedClaims.claim: the source-use verdict each licence family carries
judgedClaims.recordedIn: a tracked table of one row per family, each row carrying its reason
judgedClaims.whyNoSecondReading: this is the decision that moves artifacts between prohibited and cleared, and it sits one function below the family test; flipping one line moves 65 artifacts without moving a single family

judgedClaims.claim: whether an author reserved their assets apart from their code
judgedClaims.recordedIn: a column beside each distinct declared string
judgedClaims.whyNoSecondReading: a reservation is a statement in prose the author wrote, and no count over the artifact contradicts a wrong reading of it
